paperTitle: 2026年6月大学英语四级真题（第3套）
passage:
P1 After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.

P2 Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal(相互的). Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.

P3 In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found. When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us. But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. The team developed leaflets(传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force. They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas. The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.

P4 Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards. Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it. They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.

P5 The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas. Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.

questions.q: What is the finding of a recent study in Nature?
options: People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers.
People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us.
People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too.
People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings.
questions.explain:
【判型】What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? 直接要求提取 recent study in Nature 的具体结论，不涉及全文主旨或作者态度。

【拆句】What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? 是主系表结构的特殊疑问句，主语为 the finding of a recent study in Nature，结构平铺直叙，无隐藏否定或比较陷阱。 51. What is the finding of a recent study in Nature? A) People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers. B) People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us. C) People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too. D) People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings.

【定位】After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. 在了解到一个陌生人的一些细节后，我们错误地认为他们也了解我们。

【选项】A) 比较结构警惕对象与方向 People are more honest with those who know them than with total strangers. 把 原文的诚实对象从陌生人偷换成熟人，并将比较对象反向设置。 B) 无中生有 People we want to have detailed information about are keen to know about us. 中的 want 与 keen 是原文没有的主观意愿，属于无中生有。 C) ✓ 正确 After finding out details about a stranger ↔People who get to know about a person we mistakenly think that they also know about us ↔ wrongly assume the person knows them too People who get to know about a person wrongly assume the person knows them too. 与 After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. 在语义上完全等价，仅做了代词和词汇替换。 D) 偷换概念 People who are familiar with each other tend to behave honestly in their everyday dealings. 将原文的 stranger 替换为 familiar with each other，把研究对象 从陌生人之间的错觉改为熟人之间的日常行为。 关于社会关系是相互的这一假设，文章是怎么说的？ A) 它是特例，而不是惯例。 B) 它并非在每种情况下都成立。 C) 它不适用于复杂的关系。 D) 在单向社会关系中，这一假设更加准确。

questions.q: What does the passage say about the assumption that social relationships are reciprocal?
options: It is more the exception than the rule.
It does not hold true in every situation.
It does not apply to complex relationships.
It is more accurate in one-sided social ties.
questions.explain:
【判型】What does the passage say about the assumption... 要求回到原文找关于该 assumption 的具体描述，属于局部信息提取。

【拆句】What does the passage say about the assumption that social relationships are reciprocal? 中 that 引导同位语从句修饰 assumption，整体是主谓宾结构，无复杂从句 嵌套。 52. What does the passage say about the assumption that social relationships are reciprocal? A) It is more the exception than the rule. B) It does not hold true in every situation. C) It does not apply to complex relationships. D) It is more accurate in one-sided social ties.

【定位】Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal. Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn't know you at all. 过去的研究发现，我们倾向于认为社会关系是相互的。大多数时候这一假设是准确的：你视 为朋友的人通常也视你为朋友。但有时社会关系更单向：例如，你可能了解到一个根本不认 识你的陌生人的某些事情。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 It is more the exception than the rule. 表示互惠假设多为例外，但原文说 Most of the time 是准确的，因此该选项与原文相反。 B) ✓ 正确 Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided ↔It does not hold true in every situation. It does not hold true in every situation. 没有绝对化，也没有扩大范围，恰好对应 Most of the time... But sometimes... 的语义。 C) 无中生有 It does not apply to complex relationships. 提到复杂关系，但原文只讨论 one- sided ties，并未对关系复杂程度分类。 D) 与原文相反 It is more accurate in one-sided social ties. 与原文相反，原文指出 one-sided ties 正是假设不准确的例外情况。 Anuj Shah 和 Michael LaForest 想 выяс清关于社会关系是相互的这一看法的什么问题？ A) 它是否可以消除对社会关系的误解。 B) 它是否有助于发展自己与陌生人的关系。 C) 它是否有助于加强人际关系。 D) 它是否可能导致对陌生人的错误假设。

questions.q: What did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest want to find out about the belief that social relationships
options: Whether it may resolve misunderstandings about social ties.
Whether it could help develop one's relationships with strangers.
Whether it could help strengthen interpersonal relationships.
Whether it may lead to false assumptions about a stranger.
questions.explain:
【判型】What did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest want to find out... 聚焦于研究者的研究意 图，属于局部细节。

【拆句】What did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest want to find out about the belief that social relationships are reciprocal? 中 that social relationships are reciprocal 为同位语 从句，修饰 belief，整体询问过去的研究目的。 53. What did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest want to find out about the belief that social relationships are reciprocal? A) Whether it may resolve misunderstandings about social ties. B) Whether it could help develop one's relationships with strangers. C) Whether it could help strengthen interpersonal relationships. D) Whether it may lead to false assumptions about a stranger.

【定位】Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social relationships are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us. 研究者 Anuj Shah 和 Michael LaForest 想知道，我们相信社会关系是互惠的这种倾向，是 否会让我们误以为一个陌生人确实认识我们。

【选项】A) 与原文相反 Whether it may resolve misunderstandings about social ties. 用 resolve misunderstandings 替换了原文的 lead to mistakenly feel，方向完全相反。 B) 无中生有 Whether it could help develop one's relationships with strangers. 中的 develop relationships 是原文没有的积极目的，属于无中生有。 C) 偷换概念 Whether it could help strengthen interpersonal relationships. 同样引入 strengthen interpersonal relationships 这一积极结果，偏离原文的研究问题。 D) ✓ 正确 our tendency to believe that social relationships are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us ↔Whether it may lead to false assumptions about a stranger. Whether it may lead to false assumptions about a stranger. 中的 it 指代 the belief that social relationships are reciprocal，lead to false assumptions 对应原文的 lead us to mistakenly feel，是对研究问题的精确概括。 Anuj Shah 和 Michael LaForest 何时在研究中发现了真正有趣的现象？ A) 在基于实验室的研究期间。 B) 在一次实地实验期间。 C) 在调查当地居民的犯罪情况时。 D) 在与附近的警察交谈时。

questions.q: When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research?
options: During lab-based studies.
During a field experiment.
While investigating local residents' crime.
While talking to police officers nearby.
questions.explain:
【判型】When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research? 要求回到原文定位 really interesting 对应的具体阶段。

【拆句】When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research? 为 when 引导的特殊疑问句，主语为研究者，谓语为 find something really interesting，结构清晰。 54. When did Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest find something really interesting in their research? A) During lab-based studies. B) During a field experiment. C) While investigating local residents' crime. D) While talking to police officers nearby.

【定位】But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. 但真正有趣的发现出现在研究者走出实验室、开展实地实验的时候。

【选项】A) 转折后的内容权重高于转折前 During lab-based studies. 对应的是前文提到的实验室研究，而原文用 But 转折指出真 正有趣的发现来自 field experiment。 B) ✓ 正确 when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment ↔ During a field experiment. During a field experiment. 与 when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. 在时间上完全对应，是对原文的精确概括。 C) 张冠李戴 While investigating local residents' crime. 对应的是第4段中居民被问及犯罪的调查环 节，而非第3段中 really interesting finding 发生的时机。 D) 偷换概念 While talking to police officers nearby. 中的 talking 是原文未描述的行为，警察只是 发放传单和卡片，并未与居民交谈。 在研究所涉及的住宅开发项目周边地区发生了什么？ A) 这些地区的犯罪案件少于对照住宅项目周边地区。 B) 这些地区见证了非法活动更快地被遏制。 C) 当地警方比以前更快地回应了犯罪投诉。 D) 当地警方与那里的居民相处得比与其他地区的居民更好。

questions.q: What happened in the areas around the housing developments subjected to the studies?
options: They saw fewer crimes than the control developments.
They witnessed a swifter elimination of illegal activities.
Local police responded more quickly to criminal complaints than before.
Local police related better to residents there than to those in other areas.
questions.explain:
【判型】What happened in the areas around the housing developments subjected to the studies? 要求提取实验后相关区域的具体变化。

【拆句】What happened in the areas around the housing developments subjected to the studies? 中 subjected to the studies 为过去分词短语作后置定语，修饰 housing developments，整体询问某地发生的事件。 55. What happened in the areas around the housing developments subjected to the studies? A) They saw fewer crimes than the control developments. B) They witnessed a swifter elimination of illegal activities. C) Local police responded more quickly to criminal complaints than before. D) Local police related better to residents there than to those in other areas.

【定位】Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments. 更令人惊讶的是，研究小组发现，在发放传单后，收到传单的小区周边地区的犯罪投诉和逮 捕数量都少于对照小区周边地区。

【选项】A) ✓ 正确 there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments ↔They saw fewer crimes than the control developments. They saw fewer crimes than the control developments. 中的 fewer crimes 对应 fewer criminal complaints and arrests，control developments 与原文原词一致，概 括准确。 B) 过度推断 They witnessed a swifter elimination of illegal activities. 中的 swifter 是原文没有的 速度含义，属于过度推断。 C) 偷换概念 Local police responded more quickly to criminal complaints than before. 把 fewer criminal complaints 错误地解释为警方响应速度提升，原文并未比较警方反应 时间。 D) 过度推断 Local police related better to residents there than to those in other areas. 把犯罪 投诉和逮捕减少归结为警民关系更好，但原文并未评价警民关系。
